title: Logarithmically Correlated Landscapes and Localization in Non-Hermitian Quasicrystals
authors: Xianqi Tong, Qifeng Ding, Xiaosen Yang
abstract: We study a one-dimensional Hatano-Nelson ring whose nonreciprocal hopping is quasiperiodically modulated through zero. A gauge transformation maps every eigenstate onto a single spatial envelope, whose logarithm becomes a deterministic, logarithmically correlated field once the hopping vanishes along the quasiperiodic orbit. We derive an exact Fourier representation and prove that the landscape variance grows logarithmically with system size, with a stiffness set by the modulation power and the arithmetic of the incommensurate frequency. The extended phase terminates at an algebraic boundary given by Jensen's formula. Inside the singular regime, localization requires the stiffness to exceed a critical threshold: above it, the wavefunction weight concentrates on the few highest landscape peaks and the state is localized; below it, the weight spreads over too many competing peaks and the state is a critical multifractal. The extreme-value statistics are anomalous: peak gaps grow as a power of the logarithm of rank, with an exponent that encodes the continued-fraction type of the frequency, distinct from the Anderson, Aubry-André, and random-gauge universality classes. The stiffness adds across channels in multiband lattices, and all signatures survive percent-level component disorder, placing the mechanism within reach of nonreciprocal topolectrical circuits.
summary: This paper analyzes wave function localization in non-Hermitian quasicrystals where hopping amplitudes modulate through zero. By mapping the system onto a logarithmically correlated potential landscape, the authors derive a critical stiffness threshold that dictates whether the state localizes or remains multifractal. The resulting signatures—including unique gap scaling laws—provide a powerful diagnostic tool for understanding complex quantum transport in engineered non-Hermitian systems.
main_problem: The study investigates localization phenomena in non-Hermitian quantum systems subjected to quasiperiodically modulated hopping that passes through zero (a singular regime). The goal is to characterize the resulting wave function behavior based on system parameters.
main_result: Localization occurs only when a derived 'stiffness' factor exceeds a critical threshold, leading to distinct signatures like super-logarithmic gap scaling in extreme-value statistics. This mechanism is robust and differs from standard Anderson or Aubry-André universality classes.
method: The authors use gauge transformations to map the non-Hermitian system onto an effective potential landscape whose variance grows logarithmically with system size, allowing for rigorous mathematical analysis of localization criteria.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional Hatano-Nelson ring with quasiperiodically modulated nonreciprocal hopping. The Hamiltonian involves terms like $t \pm \mu \cos(2\pi \alpha n + 	heta)$, placing it in the realm of non-Hermitian quasicrystals.
key_observables: Landscape Variance ($	ext{Var}(\xi) \propto \ln L$), Stiffness ($g$), Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR), and the scaling exponent ($\gamma_\alpha$) governing peak gaps.
important_parameters: Modulation depth ($\mu$), mean hopping ($t$), quasiperiodic frequency ($\alpha$), and the stiffness factor $g$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the non-Hermiticity into a gauge field whose fluctuations determine localization, assuming the dominant contribution to eigenstate modulus comes from this singular factor.
figures_summary: Figures compare localization mechanisms (NHSE vs. Anderson), show energy spectra and intensity profiles under periodic/open boundary conditions, and illustrate the phase diagram showing variance scaling versus system size.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the model via a gauge transformation, derives the logarithmic growth of landscape variance in the singular regime ($|\mu| > |t|$), defines the localization criterion based on stiffness $g$, and finally characterizes this mechanism using unique super-logarithmic gap statistics.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding how non-Hermiticity, combined with quasiperiodicity, generates novel forms of spectral localization that are mathematically distinct from standard models. The connection to robust physical circuits (topolectrical) is highly relevant for AMO/Quantum Optics applications.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Three localization mechanisms in one-dimensional non-Hermitian lattices. (a) Conventional skin effect under open boundaries. (b) Anderson or Aubry-Andr´e localization driven by an on-site potential. (c) This work: a singular quasiperiodic gauge field builds a deterministic log-correlated landscape on a closed ring.

FIG. 2. Hatano-Nelson ring with quasiperiodic nonreciprocal hopping at t = 1, µ = 2.5, p = 2, and golden-mean frequency. (a) Energy spectrum under PBC, forming a closed loop, and under OBC, collapsing onto the real axis. (b) Eigenstate in- tensities In under PBC for three modulation phases θ; all share the same envelope. (c) Gauge field h(φ) showing log- arithmic singularities at the zeros of t + µ cos φ. Dots mark the quasiperiodic orbit samples.

FIG. 3. Landscape statistics at t = 1, µ = 2.5 unless labeled, and golden-mean frequency. (a) Stiffness g versus µ at L = 2584, averaged over 160 phases. The extended phase with g = 0 ends at µ = t; inside the singular regime, a localization threshold at g = 1/2 separates critical states at p = 1 from localized states at p ≥2. (b) Fractal dimension D2 versus 1/ ln L for several (µ, p) combinations. Stars mark the L →∞extrapolations. (c) Gap statistics ∆Mk on doubly logarithmic axes for three frequencies at L = 108–2 × 108, averaged over 48 phases.

FIG. 4. Non-Hermitian SSH chain with t1 = t2 = 1, p = 2, and golden-mean frequency. (a) Phase diagram in the (µ1, µ2) plane. Color encodes the disorder-averaged IPR and dashed lines mark the predicted boundaries. (b) Landscape variance Var(ξ) versus ln L for four representative parameter combi- nations with different total stiffness gtot. (c) Cell-resolved in- tensity In compared with the analytic two-channel envelope.

FIG. 5. Robustness of the localization mechanism at t = 1, µ = 2.5, p = 2, and golden-mean frequency. (a) Disorder- averaged IPR versus asymmetry parameter δ at two system sizes, averaged over 8 phases and 10 midspectrum states. (b) Disorder-averaged IPR versus component tolerance ϵ, av- eraged over 8 phases and 4 noise realizations.
